title: Matrix algebra and solution verification
purpose: Represent systems compactly, perform valid matrix operations, and recognize the limits of inversion and rounded computation.

lessons.title: Matrix dimensions and operations
lessons.objective: Determine whether matrix operations are defined and compute sums, scalar products, and matrix products correctly.
lessons.coverage: Row/column indexing, dimensions, equality, addition, scalar multiplication, row-by-column multiplication, identity and zero matrices, and noncommutativity.
lessons.activity: Choose an output entry, highlight its contributing row and column, predict the dot product, and compare A*B with B*A when both exist.
families: Classify operation compatibility and output dimensions
Compute small products and identify a counterexample to commutativity
lessons.generatorRules: Use 2x2, 2x3, and 3x2 matrices with small integers. Keep undefined operations distinct from zero matrices; include cases where only one product order is possible.
lessons.commonError: Multiplying corresponding entries, reversing dimensions, or assuming A*B=B*A.
lessons.feedback: Write the inner dimensions and expand one row-column product term by term.
lessons.checkpoint: Dimension compatibility, addition/scaling, multiplication, and noncommutativity.

lessons.title: Augmented matrices and row reduction
lessons.objective: Represent a linear system as an augmented matrix and use valid row operations to classify and solve it.
lessons.coverage: Variable order, row swaps, nonzero row scaling, row replacement, pivots, echelon forms, back substitution, free variables, and inconsistent rows.
lessons.activity: Perform explicit row operations through dropdowns and numeric fields; preview the new row, undo an operation, and compare the matrix with the equivalent equations.
families: Complete a valid elimination path for a 2x2 or 3x3 system
Classify solution sets from echelon forms including free variables and contradictions
lessons.generatorRules: Record exact rational entries and operations. Disallow scaling a row by zero and choose a pivoting strategy when the apparent pivot is zero.
lessons.commonError: Changing only part of a row, dividing by a zero pivot, or assuming a row of zeros means every variable is zero.
lessons.feedback: Show the equivalent equation for the row and identify whether a pivot or a free variable remains.
lessons.checkpoint: Matrix translation, valid row operation, solution extraction, and free-variable/inconsistency interpretation.

lessons.title: Determinants and inverse matrices
lessons.objective: Use a 2x2 determinant to decide invertibility, compute an inverse when it exists, and solve a system by multiplication in the correct order.
lessons.coverage: ad-bc, singular matrices, the 2x2 inverse formula, A inverse times b, verification with identity products, and inverse computation by row operations as an extension within the lesson.
lessons.activity: Predict whether two rows provide independent information, compute the determinant, and multiply a proposed inverse by the original matrix to check it.
families: Classify and invert a nonsingular 2x2 matrix
Audit a proposed inverse or solve A*x=b while preserving multiplication order
lessons.generatorRules: Generate singular examples deliberately and never divide by their determinant. Use bounded determinants for hand arithmetic; a singular matrix alone does not decide whether A*x=b is inconsistent.
lessons.commonError: Using bc-ad, inverting each entry, writing b*A inverse, or assuming singular always means no solution.
lessons.feedback: Check the identity product and compare the coefficient matrix with the augmented system.
lessons.checkpoint: Determinant, inverse, matrix solution, and interpretation of a singular case.

lessons.title: Choosing methods and checking numerical results
lessons.objective: Select an appropriate system solution method, use Cramer's rule for a small nonsingular case, and verify a rounded result using residuals.
lessons.coverage: Two-variable Cramer's rule, replacement-column order, comparison with elimination and inversion, residual vector A*x-b, rounding effects, and why a small residual alone does not guarantee insensitivity to data changes.
lessons.activity: Compare exact and rounded solutions for two systems, perturb a supplied measurement, and explain which solution changes more without requiring a condition-number calculation.
families: Solve a 2x2 system using replacement determinants and check by substitution
Compare candidate solutions using residuals and interpret a supplied sensitivity example
lessons.generatorRules: Require nonzero determinant for Cramer's rule. Supply the perturbed comparison data and use exact reference solutions; formal numerical analysis stays outside the completion requirements.
lessons.commonError: Replacing the wrong column, treating a rounded answer as exact, or claiming numerical stability from one small residual.
lessons.feedback: Label each variable's column, compute both original equations at the candidate, and compare the size of input and output changes.
lessons.checkpoint: Replacement determinant, solution, residual verification, and method/rounding interpretation.

anchor.prompt: For A=[[2,1],[1,-1]] and b=[7,2], find the determinant, inverse, and solution of A*x=b.
anchor.answer: det(A)=-3. A inverse=[[1/3,1/3],[1/3,-2/3]]. The solution is [3,1], with residual [0,0].

moduleExit: Demonstrate dimensions, valid row operations, singular-case reasoning, and residual checking. Matrix algebra cannot be reduced to memorizing the 2x2 inverse formula.
